 Christian Pulisic wanted to send Mauricio Pochettino off in style on Tuesday evening, and he did just that with one of the best goals of his USMNT career.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In Pochettino's final game, the United States men were looking to wrap up a spot in the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals. They had already won 6-0 in the first leg in Miami, taking a huge aggregate lead with them to Cincinnati for the second leg.
 As the U.S. dominated proceedings in the first half, they snatched the lead when Pulisic sent the attending fans into dreamland with a stunning bicycle kick goal to put the USMNT on the scoreboard first.
 The incredible strike, his third of the two-legged matchup, put the U.S. ahead and all but wrapped up their place in the semifinals this March.
 MORE: Mauricio Pochettino tells Pep Guardiola to "take it" about the USMNT job 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Highlights of Christian Pulisic goal vs. Haiti
 Fans were left stunned when, in the 25th minute, Pulisic opened the scoring in the second leg against Haiti with a sensational bicycle kick.
 U.S. Soccer posted a clip with a number of different angles of the goal.
 Here is the call from legendary Spanish-language broadcaster Andres Cantor on Telemundo.
 And here is the Spanish-language call of the goal from Fox Deportes Guatemala.
 Christian Pulisic on fire for USMNT, AC Milan
 After a relatively quiet 2026 FIFA World Cup on home soil, in which Christian Pulisic did not score, he has come back to life to begin the 2030 Wold Cup cycle.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With the CONCACAF Nations League, Pulisic has returned to one of his favorite competitions, as his three goals in the two quarterfinal legs against Haiti give him nine goals in 17 career Nations League matches.
 Overall, Pulisic now has 35 goals in 92 career international matches.
 He is also in good form for his club AC Milan, with three goals in his last four Serie A matches, including one against derby rivals Inter Milan on October 31.
